correctness.rationale: At the frozen RESULT.md proof, thin SVD and orthogonal Gaussian invariance give H^2/||E||^2=(h_1^2+r^4 h_2^2)/(h_1^2+r^2 h_2^2). For 0<r<t<1 the event is |h_1/h_2|<r sqrt((t^2-r^2)/(1-t^2)); the standard Cauchy ratio gives its exact probability. The identity t^4/4-r^2(t^2-r^2)=(r^2-t^2/2)^2 proves global uniqueness of the maximizing ratio, achieved by diag(1,t/sqrt(2)); inverse solving t^4=4c_delta^2(1-t^2) proves sharp calibration. Explicitly excludes rank>2, complex/projection-free probes and dependent reuse. Independently checked rational square identities and Gaussian Monte Carlo at several thresholds; sampling corroborates, rather than proves, this continuum law.
